title: Fix deadlock in quality gate run cancelation + add regression test
author: Jordan Lee
description: Context: During internal beta for Optimize quality gates, we hit a rare deadlock when a gate run is canceled while the eval-harness callback is concurrently finalizing results. This surfaced as gate runs stuck in RUNNING forever (no terminal state), blocking apply/rollout, and caused a near-miss where a canary pipeline sat waiting until manual intervention. Root cause is a lock ordering inversion between (a) GateRun state transitions in Optimize (DB row lock + in-memory mutex keyed by gate_run_id) and (b) cancelation handler that attempted to revoke the eval job and update state while holding the per-run mutex, while the callback path held the DB transaction and attempted to acquire the same mutex to emit completion events. Fix: remove the cross-path mutex dependency by (1) making cancelation idempotent and purely DB-driven, using a single conditional UPDATE that only transitions RUNNING->CANCEL_REQUESTED, (2) moving external side effects (eval-harness revoke + audit event emission) out of the DB transaction, and (3) ensuring the callback finalization path uses compare-and-set semantics and respects CANCEL_REQUESTED by transitioning to CANCELED (with artifacts preserved) instead of writing PASSED/FAILED. Also adds a deterministic regression test that simulates callback + cancel racing under a controllable scheduler and asserts we always reach a terminal state within a bounded time. Post-incident notes: This was first observed in eu-west during GPU scarcity where retries stretched gate duration, increasing the probability of cancel/finish overlap; see incident thread #incidents 1764369002 and support ticket SUP-18487 for timeline. This PR is a hotfix targeted for beta stability and does not change gate policy/threshold behavior.
commits: optimize/gates: make cancelation transition DB-conditional and idempotent
optimize/gates: move eval-harness revoke and audit emit out of txn
optimize/gates: callback finalization respects CANCEL_REQUESTED state
tests: add race regression test for cancel vs finalize (deterministic scheduler)
docs: add brief internal note on cancelation semantics + operator guidance
implementation_notes: Behavioral changes: (1) Cancel requests are now represented as a durable intermediate state CANCEL_REQUESTED rather than an in-process flag; (2) The only paths allowed to write terminal states are the callback finalizer and the cancelation reconciler, both using conditional updates on expected prior state; (3) If eval-harness returns success/failure after a cancel request, we record the metrics/artifacts but the gate_run state becomes CANCELED (reason=canceled_by_user or canceled_by_system) to avoid unblocking apply based on results the user intended to cancel. Safety: This maintains defense-in-depth at the apply boundary (apply still requires PASSED or explicit override), while ensuring cancelation cannot wedge the system. Observability: Added a counter for gate_run_cancel_finalize_race_total with tags {resolved_state, path} and a histogram for cancel_reconcile_latency_ms; both are low-cardinality and intended for beta-only dashboards (will keep if useful).
review_conversation: Olivia Grant: The fix makes sense. One question: in the callback finalizer, you’re conditionally updating RUNNING->PASSED/FAILED, but now also checking CANCEL_REQUESTED. Can we end up in CANCEL_REQUESTED forever if revoke fails? Please confirm reconciler covers that case.

Jordan Lee (author): Yep. The reconciler runs on a short interval and moves CANCEL_REQUESTED->CANCELED regardless of revoke outcome (revoke is best-effort). We persist revoke_error in metadata and emit an audit event so oncall can see it, but we never block the terminal transition on external revoke.

Sean Gallagher: Please add a bounded-time assertion in the regression test (no infinite waits) and ensure the test fails deterministically if the scheduler doesn’t progress. We’ve had flakes from concurrency tests.

Jordan Lee (author): Done. Test now uses DeterministicScheduler with an explicit step budget; if terminal state isn’t reached within 200 steps, it fails with a dump of executed tasks and last observed state.

Michael Nguyen: DB-side: The conditional UPDATE introduces a new state value. Did you update the enum / check constraint migration and backfill for existing rows? Also ensure read paths don’t choke on unknown state.

Jordan Lee (author): Added migration to extend the gate_run_state enum with CANCEL_REQUESTED and CANCELED (CANCELED existed logically but wasn’t in the DB enum everywhere). Read paths already treat unknown as RUNNING; updated to treat CANCEL_REQUESTED as running-ish but non-applyable. Also added a small backfill to normalize legacy 'CANCELLED' typo to 'CANCELED'.
Sahana Iyer: CI concern: any changes to the callback signature / retry behavior? I want to ensure eval-harness doesn’t need a coordinated deploy.
Jordan Lee (author): No contract changes. We only changed how we handle callback ordering on our side. Callback payload unchanged. This is safe to roll independently.
Olivia Grant: Approving. Please link the incident note in the PR description so folks can find context later.
Jordan Lee (author): Linked to #incidents thread id in description and added a short internal note under services/optimize/docs/quality_gates_cancelation.md.
release_notes: Internal beta hotfix: Fixes rare deadlock where canceling a running quality gate could leave it stuck in RUNNING. Gate runs now reliably transition to a terminal state (CANCELED) even when cancel and completion race. Adds regression test to prevent reintroduction.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash; deployed to staging immediately after merge and rolled into beta canary the same day. Oncall verified no increase in stuck RUNNING gate runs over 24h.
